signals.title: USD/JPY — Cross-Asset Vol + Rate Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.91, holding below its 20-day SMA at 158.62 while equity markets suffer a broad selloff, with VIX surging 26.20% intraday to 35.9 (high volatility / fear). Cross-asset correlation between USD/JPY and VIX sits at -0.054 versus its 252-day norm of +0.266 (z = -2.24σ), indicating that typical JPY safe-haven appreciation is failing to materialize cleanly despite acute risk-off sentiment. Options markets reflect heavy downside demand, with USD/JPY 25-delta risk reversal showing a strong put skew of -1.77 alongside 7.5% 1M IV versus 5.5% HV30 (VRP +1.9%). Leveraged funds COT positioning shows JPY net short at -29,545 contracts (85th percentile of its 52-week range), leaving the carry trade vulnerable to liquidity squeezes if equity stress forces deleveraging. However, the +268bp SOFR-TONA OIS carry differential and 275bp Fed-BoJ policy spread continue to support USD/JPY on dips while VIX remains elevated. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; severe cross-asset vol stress competes directly with a resilient carry premium. Catalyst: Tokyo CPI release at 05:00 UTC. Risk: VIX extends above 40.0, accelerating forced carry unwinds and driving spot below SMA50 support at 157.95.

signals.title: NZD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: NZD/CHF trades with a pronounced negative structural bias, driven by a G10 1W performance spread of 1.098% between CHF (leader +0.617%, n=6) and NZD (laggard -0.481%, n=4). Real macroeconomic data momentum reinforces this divergence: SNB Vice President Martin highlighted second-round inflation risks following a 1.5% print, supporting SNB hike expectations, while Switzerland's Economic Surprise Index stands at a strong positive +28.0. Conversely, New Zealand's ESI registers a negative -15.4, reflecting persistent macroeconomic data misses. Leveraged funds COT positioning shows CHF net shorts at extreme historical lows (-21,646 contracts, 2nd percentile of 52-week range, z = -1.96), while NZD positioning remains net short at -23,862 contracts (23rd percentile). The +275bp NZD/CHF carry advantage (RBNZ 2.75% vs SNB 0.00%) fails to defend the pair against safe-haven capital flows into CHF during global risk-off sessions. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/CHF; CHF data outperformance and safe-haven flows override NZD carry advantage. Catalyst: SNB policy decision on 10 Dec. Risk: Sharp rebound in global risk appetite compresses CHF outperformance below the 0.80% G10 spread threshold.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning Extreme + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6652, remaining trapped below its SMA20/50/200 moving average cluster (0.6883/0.6964/0.7046) in a firm technical downtrend. Institutional COT data shows leveraged funds holding net long AUD positions of +26,143 contracts, but WoW flows contracted by -15,052 contracts, signalling significant late-trend positioning exhaustion. Retail market sentiment exhibits an extreme long bias at 87% (13% short), setting up a structural divergence as retail accounts attempt to catch the falling pair against broader institutional liquidation. Fundamentals offer little support, as Australia flash PMI dropped to 46.1—its fastest private sector contraction in five years—while the Australia ESI sits at -9.6. Although RBA's 4.85% rate vs Fed's 4.00% provides an 85bp carry advantage (SOFR vs AONIA OIS spread at -94bp), risk-off market conditions limit carry demand. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD; institutional liquidation and weak PMI data outweigh carry support. Catalyst: RBA policy meeting on 8 Dec. Risk: Sharp reversal in global risk sentiment drives a short-squeeze back toward SMA20 resistance at 0.6883.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Yield Momentum + Technical Uptrend
signals.text: USD/CAD holds at 1.4313, maintaining an uptrend above its SMA20 (1.4140), SMA50 (1.4131), and SMA200 (1.3929) moving average structure. The Fed at 4.00% versus BoC at 2.50% establishes a 150bp policy differential favoring USD (+136bp SOFR-CORRA OIS spread), providing a durable carry floor. Recent Canadian macroeconomic releases show elevated slack, with Canadian unemployment ticking up to 6.7% (a 3.00σ surprise beat in joblessness), which strengthens bets for BoC rate cuts. 2Y yield momentum reflects this bias, with CA-US 2Y spreads widening in USD's favor to -149bp. Retail positioning sits at an extreme 92% short (8% long), creating contrarian upside risk as retail traders continuously fight the established multi-month trend. Options volatility shows low hedging panic, with USD/CAD 1M IV at 8.2% vs 7.9% HV30 (VRP +0.4%). Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; central bank policy divergence and contrarian retail positioning sustain the bid. Catalyst: BoC Governor Macklem speech at 23:19 UTC. Risk: A rebound in WTI crude oil above $88/bbl strengthens CAD fundamentals and breaks SMA20 support at 1.4140.
